title: Fingolimod Alleviates Neuroinflammation and Blood-Brain Barrier Disruption in Epilepsy by Upregulating S1PR5 and Inhibiting the Rho/ROCK/NF-kappaB Pathway.
authors: Zhang, Chen; Duan, Yanli; Ma, Mengmeng; Xu, Lin; Jin, Wei-Na; Zhang, Zhuoran
one_liner_zh: 该文研究芬戈莫德通过S1PR5调控Rho/ROCK/NF-kappaB通路缓解癫痫神经炎症和血脑屏障损伤，核心为药物-受体结合与信号通路，不涉及蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合建模，与本课题无关。
abstract: OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to clarify the role of sphingosine-1-phosphate receptor 5 (S1PR5) in epileptic pathogenesis and the mechanism by which fingolimod exerts anti-epileptic effects, with a focus on neuroinflammation and blood-brain barrier (BBB) disruption. METHODS: Multi-omics integration and machine learning were used to identify S1PR5 as a key candidate gene. Molecular docking was performed to verify the binding affinity between fingolimod and S1PR5. AAV-mediated S1PR5 overexpression was conducted in mouse hippocampi before kainic acid (KA) administration. KA-induced epileptic mice were randomly divided into control, model, and fingolimod intervention groups. Behavioral tests, qRT-PCR, Western blot, immunofluorescence, ELISA, and Evans Blue assay were used for evaluations. RESULTS: S1PR5 expression was significantly downregulated in both epileptic patients and mouse hippocampi. Fingolimod bound stably to S1PR5 in silico. S1PR5 overexpression attenuated neuronal loss, microglial activation, and epileptic seizures in KA-treated mice, confirming that S1PR5 exerts protective effects in epilepsy. Fingolimod intervention upregulated S1PR5 expression, inhibited abnormal activation of the Rho/ROCK/NF-kappaB pathway, restored tight junction proteins (Claudin-5 and ZO-1), reduced BBB leakage, and lowered proinflammatory cytokines (TNF-alpha, IL-1beta, IL-6). These changes were accompanied by alleviated seizure severity and frequency. CONCLUSION: S1PR5 serves as a protective regulator in epilepsy. Fingolimod exerts anti-epileptic effects by upregulating S1PR5, thereby inhibiting the Rho/ROCK/NF-kappaB pathway, reducing neuroinflammation, and preserving BBB integrity. These findings support S1PR5 as a promising target and provide a mechanistic basis for repurposing fingolimod in epilepsy therapy.
abstract_zh: 目的：本研究旨在阐明1-磷酸鞘氨醇受体5（S1PR5）在癫痫发病机制中的作用，以及芬戈莫德发挥抗癫痫作用的机制，重点关注神经炎症和血脑屏障（BBB）破坏。方法：采用多组学整合和机器学习方法，将S1PR5鉴定为关键候选基因。通过分子对接验证芬戈莫德与S1PR5之间的结合亲和力。在海马体内注射红藻氨酸（KA）前，通过AAV介导S1PR5过表达。将KA诱导的癫痫小鼠随机分为对照组、模型组和芬戈莫德干预组。采用行为学测试、qRT-PCR、Western blot、免疫荧光、ELISA和伊文思蓝实验进行评估。结果：在癫痫患者和小鼠海马中，S1PR5表达均显著下调。芬戈莫德在计算机模拟中与S1PR5稳定结合。S1PR5过表达减轻了KA处理小鼠的神经元丢失、小胶质细胞活化和癫痫发作，证实S1PR5在癫痫中发挥保护作用。芬戈莫德干预上调S1PR5表达，抑制Rho/ROCK/NF-kappaB通路的异常激活，恢复紧密连接蛋白（Claudin-5和ZO-1），减少BBB渗漏，并降低促炎细胞因子（TNF-alpha、IL-1beta、IL-6）水平。这些变化伴随癫痫发作严重程度和频率的减轻。结论：S1PR5在癫痫中作为保护性调节因子。芬戈莫德通过上调S1PR5发挥抗癫痫作用，从而抑制Rho/ROCK/NF-kappaB通路，减少神经炎症，并维持BBB完整性。这些发现支持S1PR5作为有前景的靶点，并为芬戈莫德在癫痫治疗中的再利用提供了机制基础。
